content.en: Shanta came to us a few months ago; she was referred to Saheli by another organization. When Shanta walked in at the door, she looked like an abject sight-- dishevelled, distraught and when she started talking, she was never far from tears.

"I was married in 1978-I saw Madan and Madan saw me; we fell in love and in spite of strong opposition from our families, we were married-we are from different communities, you see, so the elders were very strongly against our marriage-

"Eventually, when we started our household, every- thing was perfect. Our first child, a daughter, was born in 1980. Our second daughter came in 1982, and our son in 1985. Outwardly we gave the impression of a happy family-but this was only a facade, because an insidious rot had set in, which was gnawing at the very foundations of our lives.

"My husband, apparently, was not satisfied with what he had-a wife, three children and an income of Rs. 10,000/- per month. So he started looking for fresh amusements until he found his entertainment in a series of other women. He began taunting me on my inability to produce more sons--You have two daughters and one son-you are incapable of bearing male children".

...only one son? My friends have all sons and you have produced only one' were taunts that filled my ears, and finally, he turned his taunts and threats into actualities, and the ever-changing series of women friends he would bring over to my house, and entertain increased.

"Ultimately, the 'other' women were occupying my bed and home and I was subjected to all manner of physical abuse. He kept telling me that I should bring more and more 'gifts' from my parents and then he might and then he might consider mending his ways. My parents are old and not well off, I could not comply with his increasing demands, so the harassment grew and grew until I could stand it no more. I poured myself a glassful of Baygon spray and drank it.

"I woke up in the hospital. I had been rushed there by a badly frightened husband, who thought he would be arrested if I died in the house. No one from my house came to visit me--my two daughters had been told that I was dead. When I recovered I went to my parent's home.
"I was shattered-on the brink of breakdown, but my parents and my friends rallied and I realized that life was still worth fighting for.

"Today, I am quite a different woman-my friends and family find it hard to see the broken Shanta they knew and I have found a new meaning to life. Today, I have my two daughters with me and I am negotiating to get my son also.

"Meantime, the main thing I have learnt is that when I want to, I can do anything; I do have the strength and I will live my life in peace. If my husband cares to join me in this, I will be happy, I have the ability to get what-ever I want, for myself."
Shanta today is a completely changed woman, she came to visit the other day, I could hardly recognize her -she walked, with an air of competence.
She was on her way to take custody of her two daughters from the police station. I was worried- would she manage?
"Shall I come with you? Are you all right ?" I asked.
"I will go and see what happens. I think I can manage; if I need help, I will telephone you".
Today she is living with her parents, has found herself a job, and seems to be in full charge of the situation, because that telephone call for help has yet to come.

Shanta is one of the women who did not really want to take the path of least resistance, and do away with herself rather than find alternatives. She realized that she had more to lose-so she rallied to the medications given in the hospital. Once out from there, she had the whole-hearted support of her parents who took her home and nursed her in an atmosphere of love and safety. Apart from the support she has had from family, friends and institutions, Shanta drew on her own renewed store of strength, to fight for her rights as a woman, and today is able to go about what she needs to do for herself, by herself, secure in the knowledge that she can do whatever she wants, and that help over the rougher patches, is hers for the asking.
